proxy.heading: Custom Proxy
proxy.description: By default, Proxy mode uses the built-in PatchMan proxy. If you want full control, point Proxy mode at your own self-hosted endpoint instead.
proxy.enableDescription: When on, Proxy mode requests are sent to your endpoint instead of the PatchMan proxy.

proxyInfo.title: How the custom proxy works
proxyInfo.description: PatchMan runs in your browser, so it can't reach most APIs directly (CORS). A proxy forwards the request for you. You can point PatchMan at any HTTP server that speaks this tiny protocol.
proxyInfo.sendBody: One POST per outgoing request to your endpoint, with a JSON body:
proxyInfo.sendNote: If you set an auth header name + value in settings, PatchMan adds that single header to every request.
proxyInfo.returnBody: Always respond with HTTP 200 (use 4xx/5xx only for proxy-level errors like bad auth). Put the upstream status inside the JSON:
proxyInfo.corsBody: Your proxy must allow this origin via CORS headers:
proxyInfo.specBody: A complete specification — including how multipart uploads are encoded and a ~50 line Node.js reference implementation — is in PROXY_SPEC.md at the repo root.

integrations.heading: Integrations
integrations.description: External services PatchMan can talk to on your behalf.
integrations.signInPrompt: Sign in to PatchMan to connect a GitLab account. Local mode is fully offline and integrations need an account so the link can be remembered across devices.

gitlab.description: Import collections from a GitLab repo and push edits back as merge requests.
gitlab.approvePrompt: You will be sent to {{host}} to approve PatchMan once. After that this view updates and you are not asked again.
gitlab.disconnectConfirm: Disconnect GitLab? You will need to reconnect to push collections back to a repo.

mcp.heading: MCP
mcp.description: Let AI clients (Claude, MCP Inspector) drive PatchMan through the Model Context Protocol. They can do exactly what you can do by hand — scoped to your account.
mcp.twoSetups: Two setups expose the same tools and can run side by side in Claude — add either or both. They register under distinct names: {{remote}} (remote) and {{local}} (this device).
mcp.remoteReach: Reaches whatever the PatchMan server can reach; works anywhere.
mcp.remoteSignIn: Sign in to PatchMan to create MCP tokens. Tokens are tied to your account so an MCP client can act on your behalf.
mcp.copyTokenNow: Copy this token now — it will not be shown again.
mcp.clientHint: Cursor & VS Code open via deep link. For Claude, paste the copied command (Claude Code) or config into claude_desktop_config.json (Claude Desktop).
mcp.noTokensEmpty: No tokens yet. Create one above to connect an MCP client.
mcp.tokenBakedIn: Your new token is baked in.
mcp.swapPlaceholder: Swap the placeholder for a token (create one above — it is shown only once).
mcp.tokenPlaceholder: <paste a pmcp_ token — create one above>
mcp.localReach: Reaches localhost and resources only this machine can reach; requires the PatchMan desktop app to be running.
mcp.localConfigNote: No token needed — the bridge self-discovers the running app. Registers as {{local}}, so it coexists with the remote {{remote}} setup above.
mcp.keepAppRunning: Keep the PatchMan desktop app running for this connection to work.
mcp.bridgeNotReady: The local bridge isn't ready yet. Reopen this panel after the app finishes starting.
mcp.configFileMac: Config file (macOS): {{path}}. Fully restart Claude Desktop after editing it.
mcp.revokeConfirm: Revoke "{{name}}"? Any MCP client using it will stop working immediately.
mcp.tokenCreatedDesc: Copy it now — it is shown only once.

perms.title: Tool permissions
perms.description: Choose which tools each token can use. All tools are on by default.
perms.connectionsNote: Turning off “Database queries” hides run_db_query; the read-only list of connections stays under “Connections”.
perms.empty: No tokens yet. Create one in the Tokens tab first.

data.heading: Data
data.description: Where the app reads and writes your collections, environments, and test cases.
data.webOnly: The web build always reads your remote account. Switching between a remote and an embedded data store is a desktop-only feature — install the desktop app to use it offline.
data.localModeDescription: You're working without an account, so all data lives in the embedded SQLite database.
data.localModeSignInHint: Sign in or create an account to enable a remote data source and the local↔remote merge tool.
data.remoteDetail: Reads and writes the prod backend. Use this when you want your work to stay in your account and visible everywhere you sign in.
data.localSub: Embedded SQLite · stays on this Mac
data.localDetail: Reads and writes the embedded backend that ships with the desktop app. Useful when you're offline or want to test against data that shouldn't touch your account. Changes here don't sync back automatically — use the merge tool below to combine them.
data.localWarning: You're logged in as <mono>{{email}}</mono> but the app is reading the embedded database. Anything you change here stays on this Mac until you merge it back.
data.mergeDescription: Compute the diff between your embedded SQLite and your remote account, then show the same merge preview that runs after a fresh login. Useful when you've made changes in local mode and want to review what would push or pull.
data.resetDescription: If the app is misbehaving or keeps crashing on launch, you can reset your local session. This only clears the data cached on this device — your remote workspaces, collections, and other data are not affected. You may need to sign in again.
data.whiteboardsNotSynced: Some whiteboards couldn't be synced — your server doesn't support whiteboard sync yet. Try again after it updates.

updates.heading: Updates
updates.webOnly: Auto-updates only apply to the desktop app. The web build refreshes automatically when you reload.
updates.currentVersion: Current version <mono>{{version}}</mono>. New releases are signed and verified before install.

about.heading: About
about.supportBody: Ping the <chan>#patchman-support</chan> channel on Slack — bug reports, feature requests, and quick usage questions all land there.
about.desktopPitch: The desktop app runs a local backend — offline access, faster requests, and full QA tooling without an account.

keymap.heading: Keyboard shortcuts
keymap.description: A reference of the shortcuts PatchMan responds to. Read-only for now — remapping is coming.
keymap.detachTab: Detach the active tab into its own window
keymap.jumpToTab: Jump to a tab by number

remote.heading: Remote backend
remote.description: The server the app connects to for sign-in and shared data.
remote.duplicate: That backend is already in the list
remote.note: The app uses the active backend for sign-in and shared data. Switching signs you out so you can sign in again there.
remote.switchBody: You’ll be signed out and PatchMan will reconnect to {{url}}. Sign in there to continue.
remote.deleteActiveHint: Switch to another backend first to delete this one.
remote.unreachable: Couldn’t reach that backend. Check the URL and try again.
remote.notPatchman: That URL isn’t a PatchMan backend.
remote.incompatible: That backend’s version isn’t compatible with this app.

appearance.heading: Appearance
appearance.description: Pick a color theme for the app.
appearance.defaultHint: Star a theme to make it the light/dark toggle's default.
appearance.sidebarDescription: Choose which items appear in the left sidebar. All are shown by default.
